text:
liam: Hey team — customer acct 7890 reported a sudden invoice jump. They gave approximate time 2026-02-10 14:37 UTC. No error in app but they saw a ~30% token bump. Can we get what to ask them for to correlate server side usage?

carl: Quick checklist to request from customer:
- exact UTC timestamps (start/end)
- account/org id shown in billing (or last 4 of it)
- the request path (e.g., POST /v1/generate), and any request_id from their client
- a minimal repro curl or HAR
- SDK logs (console or device logs) around the time
- invoice id / billing statement screenshot
Also ask them to redact secrets.

liam: they'll likely be non-technical — want a minimal copy-pasteable instruction.

carl: send this short snippet and ask them to replace their token with REDACTED and include the last 6 chars:
```
curl -v -D headers.txt --trace-ascii trace.txt \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Explain: headers.txt will contain response headers (look for `x-request-id` or `x-rw-trace`). trace.txt has verbose TCP/HTTP traces. If they can't run curl, ask for a HAR: Chrome DevTools > Network tab > right-click > Save all as HAR with content. Remove cookies/Auth before uploading.

maya: Quick SDK/UI pointers to help them find trace tokens:
- Console: Console > Logs & Requests > click the request row > "Copy trace token" (button next to timestamp).
- Browser SDK: run in console `console.log(window.Redwood?.getTraceToken?.() || 'no-trace')`
- Node SDK: set env RW_LOG_TRACE=1, re-run the request, capture stdout.
- Android: filter logcat `adb logcat | grep RW-TRACE` or look for header `X-RW-TRACE` in OkHttp logs.
- iOS: Xcode console, filter for `RW-TRACE`, or check response header `x-rw-trace`.

maya: Header names to ask for (customer may paste any of these):
- x-request-id
- x-rw-trace
- redwood-request-id
Also check response body meta: `{"meta":{"request_id":"..."}}` if their client surface returns that.

carl: If they can produce a HAR or curl, ask them to also include:
- exact timestamps for the file (UTC)
- account id (or last 4)
- endpoint path
- invoice id or billing screenshot
Tell them: "You can safely redact Authorization but please keep header name and the last 4–6 chars of the token so we can map it."

maya: If they cannot run these, we can generate a one-time debug token from Console > Support > Create debug token and ask them to run a small repro with that token so we get server-side logs. Steps we use internally: create token, ask them to run the failing call with `Authorization: Bearer <debug-token>`, then we retrieve a debug bundle.

ops-bot: Note: pasting a debug token here will auto-open INC ticket INC-4582.

liam: Perfect. I'll message the customer with the short curl + HAR instructions and ask for timestamps + invoice id. I'll request the Console debug token only if they can't produce logs.
